narration: The biggest change in AI coding is not better autocomplete. It is software that can take a goal and carry out a sequence of actions.
voiceDirection: Strong thesis opening, calm and clear.

narration: Autocomplete stays inside the editor. You type, it predicts the next line, and you decide what to keep.
An agent can work at a wider level. It can inspect the repository, understand files, and decide which part of the codebase it needs to touch.
It can edit files, run commands, use connected tools, and check the result instead of stopping at a code suggestion.
It can also run tests and iterate when something fails. That turns coding assistance into a loop instead of a single completion.
captionText: Iteration becomes part of the workflow.

narration: That changes the developer’s job. You spend less time producing every keystroke and more time specifying the goal, constraints, and architecture.
Then you review what the agent actually changed: the diff, the tests, the permissions it used, and whether the result matches the intent.

The new software-building workflow is not just faster typing. It is giving an agent a well-scoped goal, letting it execute inside clear boundaries, and keeping human judgment around the result. That is the shift from autocomplete to agents.
captionText: Agents expand execution. Humans keep judgment.
voiceDirection: Month-end thesis close. Confident, not hype-driven.
